paper.title: A Time Series is Worth 64 Words: Long-term Forecasting with Transformers

concepts.evidence: Each input univariate time series is divided into patches that may overlap or not overlap.
concepts.annotation: Tensor unfold is the direct supervised implementation of paper patching.

concepts.evidence: Channels share one Transformer backbone while their forward processes remain independent.
concepts.annotation: Channels are folded into the batch dimension before the shared encoder.

concepts.concept: Patch projection and learnable positional encoding
concepts.evidence: Patches are linearly projected and combined with a learnable additive position encoding.
concepts.annotation: The encoder constructor creates both projection and positional encoding.

concepts.evidence: A vanilla Transformer encoder maps observed patch signals to latent representations.
concepts.annotation: The stack applies repeated encoder layers with optional residual attention.

concepts.evidence: Each attention head transforms patch representations into query, key, and value matrices.
concepts.annotation: The implementation projects Q/K/V per head and combines attention outputs.

concepts.evidence: Attention uses scaled query-key products; encoder blocks include residual connections.
concepts.annotation: This symbol computes scaled scores and optionally adds previous-layer scores.

concepts.evidence: A flatten layer followed by a linear head produces the forecast horizon.
concepts.annotation: The head flattens patch representations and applies a linear projection.

concepts.evidence: Each series is normalized before patching, with its statistics restored to predictions.
concepts.annotation: Normalization and inverse transformation form an intentional one-to-many mapping.

concepts.evidence: Randomly removed patches are reconstructed during self-supervised representation learning.
concepts.annotation: Mask creation and reconstruction head jointly implement the pretext task.

concepts.evidence: Patch-level masking requires converting each sequence into a regular sequence of patches.
concepts.annotation: A support utility rather than the conceptual model itself; retained as a boundary case.

concepts.evidence: The implementation optionally combines trend and residual forecasts around the PatchTST backbone.
concepts.annotation: Implementation extension with weak direct support in the core paper; tests low-confidence handling.

concepts.evidence: Per-channel squared forecasting errors are averaged into the overall training objective.
concepts.annotation: Loss wiring lives in training configuration, not a stable named model symbol at the frozen commit.
